notes:
Residential population: official Zensus 2022 100m population grid (Destatis), aggregated to München's 25 Stadtbezirke and surrounding Gemeinden, then redistributed within each zone proportionally to residential building footprint area (Overture Maps buildings, non-residential buildings such as police stations/courthouses/parking structures/industrial excluded via OSM tags).

Employment: real employment-at-workplace counts (Statistik 13111 "Beschäftigte am Arbeitsort", Bundesagentur für Arbeit, via regionalstatistik.de GENESIS-Online) for München and its 10 largest satellite municipalities (Dachau, Starnberg, Freising, Erding, Germering, Fürstenfeldbruck, Unterschleißheim, Unterhaching, Vaterstetten, Olching) — 8 of these 10 have official job totals, accounting for ~76.3% of the map's total modeled jobs (1,059,375 of 1,388,950). Jobs are redistributed within each municipality proportionally to the density of OSM economic POIs (shop/office/amenity tags) at 250m grid resolution, then scaled so the municipality total matches the real Beschäftigtenstatistik figure exactly. Note: the placement dropdown above ("OpenStreetMap buildings, split by size") is the closest available option — the actual mechanism weights by OSM POI count per grid cell rather than building footprint size, while still being forced to match the real government total. Remaining smaller municipalities (~185 Gemeinden/Stadtbezirke) use the same POI-density model without a real anchor total, calibrated against neighboring real data where they connect to a core municipality.

Commute flows: real municipality-to-municipality commuter tables (Statistik 19321 "Pendlerrechnung der Länder", regionalstatistik.de) exist for the same 10 core municipalities (full origin-destination pairs, not just totals), used to weight the gravity model's flow generation for those zones; remaining flows are fully estimated via the gravity model. A minimum 10km origin-destination distance is enforced, with up to 15 local retries and 40 global retries per commuter, to avoid unrealistic short trips that would walk instead of drive/take transit.

Routing: all travel times/distances computed via OSRM on the real OpenStreetMap road network (not straight-line estimates).

Special points: Munich Airport (split into Terminal 1 and Terminal 2, weighted 26%/74% based on a Lufthansa Group-published Terminal 2 traffic figure, against a 42%-transfer-passenger O&D correction from Munich Airport's 2025 Integrated Report), LMU and TU München (real enrollment figures), LMU Klinikum (real bed count × standard employment ratio) added as special demand points from officially published real-world figures, not estimated from the base model.

Data vintage: Zensus 2022 (population), Beschäftigtenstatistik/Pendlerrechnung latest available year via regionalstatistik.de (employment/commute), OSM extract and Overture Maps buildings as of build date (August 2026). — Reviewer refinements (2026-08-26): workplace intensity credited as binary_split — the OSM economic-POI density routing, scaled to match each real Beschaeftigtenstatistik municipal total exactly, is a workplace-side type signal (tehran precedent), not plain size-spreading; workplace_count stays physical_inferred with the partial-anchor coverage on record (8 of 10 core municipalities carry real totals = 76.3% of modeled jobs; the ~185 smaller Gemeinden are POI-model estimates without an anchor). Resident granularity pinned to mesh_125 per the published-grain rule (Zensus 2022 is a 100m grid); note the pipeline aggregates to Stadtbezirk/Gemeinde and respreads onto Overture residential footprints with generic weights, which is what the filed resolution/intensity answers price (bounds recorded: mesh_125 published / ~adm4 as-used anchor). O/D scored structured_marginals, not full_matrix — the real Pendlerrechnung O-D pairs cover only the 10 core municipalities (the defining flows, bale partial-coverage precedent); flows among the ~185 remaining Gemeinden are gravity-estimated, so "a full table between every pair of areas" is not met.
